x: God Almighty swore by those who rank up, those who repel, and those who recite the Reminder. As for those who rank up, they are the angels who rank up for their Lord in the heavens, and it is the plural of saffah, so saffah is the plural of plural, and this is how the people of interpretation interpreted it.
Who said that?

c: Salim bin Junada told me: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, who said:
m: Masruq used to say about al-Saffat 37:They are the angels.

m: I heard Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And those in rows, he said: God swore by creation, then creation, then creation, and those in rows: the angels in rows in the sky.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: And those in ranks, he said: They are the angels.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And those who stand in rows, he said: This is an oath by which God swore.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement, And those who drive with a driving.
Some of them said: They are the angels who drive the clouds and drive them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahidah, regarding his statement,
h

, he said: The angels.

m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who drive away with a driving away
, he said: They are the angels.

x: Others said: Rather, these are the verses of the Qur’an in which God forbade what He forbade in the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And those who forbid with a forbidding force, he said: What God forbade in the Qur’an. What is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse in our view is what Mujahid said, and those who said they are the angels, because God Almighty mentioned Himself, began the oath with a type of angels, and they are the ones in rows, according to the consensus of the people of interpretation, so what comes after it is an oath with all their types, it is more likely.

x: And his saying, Then those who recite the Reminder, means: The ones who recite the Book.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of this.
Some of them said: They are the angels.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And those who recite the Reminder, he said: The angels.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Those who recite the Reminder: they are the angels.

x: Others said: It is what is recited in the Qur’an about the report of the nations before us.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And those who recite the Reminder, he said: What is recited to you in the Qur’an of the report of the people and nations before you.

Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And those who recite the Reminder, he said: What is recited to you in the Qur’an of the report of the people and nations before you.

x: God Almighty means by His statement: Indeed, your God is One and the verses in rows, that your deity, the One whom you, O people, must worship and who deserves your sincere obedience to, is One, with no second or partner. He says: So devote your worship to Him and single Him out in obedience, and do not associate any partners with Him in your worship of Him.
And His statement,
h
Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them

, means: One, Creator of the seven heavens and what is between them of creation, and Owner of all of that, and Guardian of all of that. He says: So worship is only appropriate for one who has this description, so do not worship anyone other than Him, and do not associate with Him in your worship of Him anyone who neither harms nor benefits, nor creates anything nor negates it. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for raising the word Lord of the heavens. Some Basran grammarians said: It is raised to mean: Indeed, your God is a Lord.

Another said: It is a response to Indeed, your God is One. Then he explained One, saying: Lord of the heavens, which is a response to One. In my opinion, this statement is more likely to be correct in this regard, because the predicate is His statement to One, and His statement
h
Lord of the heavens is a translation of it and a statement that rejects its syntax
. And his saying,
h
And by the Lord of the Easts

, means: And He who directs the rising of the sun in winter and summer is its setting, and He is the one who is responsible for that and makes it right. He left out mentioning the setting because the speech indicates it, and He dispensed with mentioning the easts instead of mentioning them, since it was known that the setting is with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, your God is One. The oath was based on this: Indeed, your God is One. “Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them and Lord of the Easts.” He said: The risings of the sun in the winter and the summer.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement Lord of the Easts: He said: The Easts are three hundred and sixty Easts, and the Wests are the same, the number of days in the year.

x: And His statement, Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars, the reciters differed in their reading of His statement, indeed, indeed, the stars. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it with the adornment of the stars, adding the adornment to the stars, and lowering the stars with Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven, which is next to you, O people, and it is the world to you, by adorning it with the stars: meaning, by adorning it with the stars.

A group of the reciters of Kufa read it with the adornment of the stars, with the tanween of adornment, and lowering the stars to return it to the adornment, meaning: We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, which is the stars, as if he said: We adorned it with the stars.

c: It was narrated from some of the reciters of Kufa
m: that he would add the tanween to the adornment and the stars to the accusative, meaning: We have adorned the nearest heaven with our adornment of the stars. If the reading of the planets had been raised if the nun of adornment was added, it would not have been a mistake, and it would have been correct in Arabic, and its meaning would have been: We have adorned the lowest heaven by adorning it with the planets, meaning that the planets adorned it, and that is because adornment is a verbal noun, so it is permissible to direct it to any of these aspects that were described in Arabic. As for the reading, I like it best with the addition of adornment to the planets and the lowering of the planets, due to the soundness of its meaning in interpretation and Arabic, and it is the reading of most of the reciters in the regions, even though the tanween in adornment and the lowering of the planets is also correct in my opinion. As for the accusative in the planets and the nominative, I do not permit reading with them, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters against them, even though the syntax and meaning are correct. The Arabists differed in their interpretation of this when the word adornment is added to the planets.
b.via: some of the reciters of Kufa

x: Some of the Basran grammarians said: If it is read thus, it does not mean some of them, but rather their adornment is their beauty.
Another said: If it is read thus, it means: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven by adorning it with the planets. We have explained what is correct in this regard in our opinion.

x: And His saying,
h
And as a protection
, God Almighty says:
h
And as a protection
for the lowest heaven, We adorned it with the adornment of the stars. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement and to preserve it.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said and to preserve it, because it is a replacement of the word with the verb, as if he said: And we preserved it, preserving it.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is from the connection of adornment, Indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven to preserve it. So he inserted the waw for repetition: that is, and we adorned it to preserve it, so he made it from adornment, and we have already explained our opinion on it. The interpretation of the statement is: And to preserve it from every rebellious, evil devil, We adorned it.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, and protection, he said: its entirety is protection from every rebellious devil.

x: And his statement: They do not listen to the highest assembly the reciters differed in their reading of his statement they do not listen, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it as: they do not listen, with a soft seen from yasma'u, meaning that they listen but do not listen. The majority of the Kufic reciters read it after lam yasma'u, so the meaning is: they do not listen, then they assimilated the t into the seen and stressed it. The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it with a light pronunciation, because the reports reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from his companions, are that the devils may eavesdrop on revelation, but they are pelted with meteors so that they do not hear.
Mentioning some of the narration of that:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakee’ narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The devils had seats in the heavens. He said: They used to hear the revelation. He said: The stars did not move, and the devils did not shoot. He said: When they heard the revelation, they would come down to earth and add nine words. He said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, whenever the devil sat in his seat, a meteor would come and would not strike it until it burned him. He said: They complained about that to Satan, and he said: It is only because of something that has happened. He said: So he sent his soldiers, and behold, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was standing praying between two mountains of Nakhl - Abu Kurayb said: Wakee’ said: He meant the valley of Nakhl - he said:

c: So they returned to Satan and informed him.
m: He said: This is what has happened.
b.via: So they returned to Satan and

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi told us: Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The jinn used to ascend to the lowest heaven to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they would add nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, but as for what they added, it would be false. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they were denied their seats and mentioned that to Satan. Stars had not been shot before that, so Satan said to them: This is only because of something that has happened on earth. So he sent his soldiers, and they found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing in prayer.

c: They came to him and informed him, and he said:
m: This is the event that has happened.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The jinn had their seats, and then he mentioned something similar.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Al-Zuhri narrated to me, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: saying: A group of the Ansar narrated to me, saying: “While we were sitting one night with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he saw a star that was thrown down. He said: ‘What do you say about this star that is thrown down?’ We said: ‘A child is born, or a dead person perishes, or a king dies and a king reigns.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is not like that, but when God decreed a matter in the heaven, the bearers of the Throne would glorify God for it, and the angels below them would glorify God in response to their glorification. They would continue like that until the glorification reached the lowest heaven. The people of the lowest heaven would say to the angels below them: ‘What did you glorify God for?’ They would say: ‘We do not know. We heard the angels above us glorify God, so we glorified God in response to their glorification. But we will be asked.’ So they would ask those above them, and they would continue like that until it reached the bearers of the Throne.” The Throne, and they say: God has decreed such and such, and they inform those who are next to them about it until they reach the lowest heaven, and the jinn steal what they say, then they come down to their human allies, and they put it on their tongues based on their imagination, and they inform them about it, and some of it is true and some of it is false, and the jinn continued like this until they were hit by these meteors. Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated:

c: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali bin Hussain, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: “While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with a group of the Ansar, a star was shot and it shone. The Prophet said: ‘What did you say about something like this in the pre-Islamic era when you saw it? ’ They said: ‘We used to say: ‘A great person dies or a great person is born. ’ The maternal uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is not shot for the death or life of anyone. But when our Lord, blessed be His name, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the people of the heavens who are next to them glorify Him, then those who are next to them, until the people of this heaven exalt their glorification. Then the people of the seventh heaven ask the bearers of the Throne: ‘What did our Lord say? ’ So they inform them. Then the people of each heaven inquire, until the report reaches the people of the lowest heaven, and the devils steal the hearing, so they shoot and hurl it to their friends. Whatever they bring as it should be is true, but they add.”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Muʿammar told us: Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Ali Ibn Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with a group of his companions. A star was shot, then he mentioned something similar, except that he added to it: I said to Al-Zuhri: Were these shot during the pre-Islamic era? He said: Yes, but they became more severe when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent.”

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Asim bin Ali told us, he said: My father Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Ata bin al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The jinn had seats in heaven where they heard the revelation. When the revelation was revealed, the angels heard it in the form of iron being thrown onto a rock. When the angels heard the clang of the revelation, the angels in heaven fell on their foreheads. When the people of revelation descended upon them, they said: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They said: ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.’”
r
(Saba’: 23)

He said: They called out to each other. He said: Your Lord is the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great. He said: When He descended to the lowest heaven, they said: ‘There will be such and such death on earth, and such and such life, and such and such drought, and such and such fertility, and what does He, the Blessed and Exalted, want to do and what does He want to initiate?’ So the jinn descended and inspired their human allies about what would happen on earth. While they were like that, God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the devils were repulsed from heaven and were pelted with stars. So none of them ascended except that he was burned, and the people of the earth were terrified by what they saw in the stars, for this had never happened before, and he said: Everyone in the sky has perished, and the people of Ta’if were the first to be terrified. A man would go to his camels and slaughter a camel every day for their gods, and the owner of the sheep would go and slaughter a sheep every day, and the owner of the cows would go and slaughter a cow every day. A man said to them: Woe to you, do not waste your wealth, for your landmarks are the stars by which you are guided, and nothing of them has fallen. So they set off, having hastened with their wealth. And Satan said: Something has happened on earth, so soil from every land was brought, and no soil of any land was brought without him smelling it. When the soil of Tihamah was brought, he said: This is where the event happened. God sent a group of jinn to him while he was reciting the Quran, and they said: Indeed, we have heard an amazing Quran (al-Jinn 72:1) until he finished the verse. So they turned back to their people as warners.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, that she said:
m: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The angels descend in the clouds and mention what has been decreed in the heavens, and the devils eavesdrop and hear it and then convey it to the devils, who tell a hundred lies along with it from their own selves.’ So these reports indicate that the devils hear, but they are pelted with meteors so that they do not hear.”

x: If someone thinks that since it is in speech to, listening is more important than hearing, then the matter in this is contrary to what he thought, and that is because the Arabs say: I heard so-and-so say such-and-such, and I heard so-and-so say such-and-such, and I heard from so-and-so. The interpretation of the statement: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars and as a protection from every rebellious devil, lest he should hear the highest assembly. So if was omitted because the statement indicates it, just as it was said: Thus We have caused it to enter the hearts of the criminals, so that they will not believe in it, meaning: that they will not believe in it. If not had been in place of that, it would have been eloquent, just as it was said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray
r
(An-Nisa’: 176)
, meaning: that you will not go astray. And as He said: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you (al-Nahl 16:15), meaning: that it should not shift with you.

The Arabs sometimes make the jussive with not in such a place in a statement, so they say: I tied up the horse so that it would not get away, just as some of Banu Uqayl said: And we saw the best of friendship between us, cohabitation, and no evil would be disgusting to the perpetrator. It is narrated: He does not feel disgusted by raising it, and raising it is the language of the people of Hijaz, as it has been said.
Qatada said about this:

, he said: Lasting means constant. The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: Its meaning is: permanent and pure. This is because God said: And to Him belongs the religion, always (al-Nahl 16:52). x: His statement, Rather, I am amazed and they mock. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa recited it as: Rather, you, O Muhammad, are amazed and they mock this Quran. The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings among the readers of the regions, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
How can the one who recites them be correct when their meanings differ?

Even though their meanings differ, each of their meanings is correct. Muhammad was amazed at the grace God had given him, and the polytheists mocked him. Our Lord was amazed at the greatness of what the polytheists said about God, and the polytheists mocked what they said.
Was the revelation by one of them or by both?
The revelation by both.
How can a letter be revealed twice?

It was not revealed twice, rather it was revealed once, but He commanded him to recite by both readings. This has a place in which we will, God willing, explain it sufficiently. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

, ‘Shall we indeed abandon our gods for the sake of a mad poet?’ God Almighty says: And these polytheists from Quraysh say: Shall we abandon the worship of our gods for the sake of a mad poet? He says: To follow a mad poet - meaning by that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and we say there is no god but God.

c: As Bishr told us,
m: Qan: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And they say
, ‘Shall we abandon our gods for the sake of a mad poet?’ They mean Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: And his saying, Rather, he came with the truth. This is report from God, refuting the polytheists who said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, He is a crazy poet. They lied. Muhammad is not as they described him, that he is a crazy poet. Rather, he is a prophet of God who came with the truth from Him, which is the Qur'an that He revealed to him, and he confirmed the messengers who came before him. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Rather, he brought the truth with the Qur’an and confirmed the messengers: meaning, he confirmed the messengers who came before him.

x: God Almighty says to these polytheists from Mecca, who said about Muhammad: He is a crazy poet, “You, polytheists, will surely taste the painful punishment” in the Hereafter.
And you will not be recompensed means: and you will not be rewarded in the Hereafter if you taste the painful torment therein except the reward for what you used to do in this world, the sins of God.
And His statement,
h
Except for the sincere servants of God

, means: Except for the servants of God whom He sincerely devoted to His mercy on the day He created them, and for whom He decreed happiness in the Mother of the Book, for they will not taste the torment, because they are people of obedience to God and people of faith in Him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Except the sincere servants of God. He said: This is God’s second choice.

x: And His statement, For them is a known provision, means: These are the sincere servants of God who have a known provision, and that known provision is the fruits that God created for them in Paradise.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Those will have a known provision
in Paradise.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those will have a known provision
, he said: In Paradise.

x: His statement, Fruits, is a response to the known provision, explaining it, and that is why it was raised. And his statement,
h
And they are honored
, means: And they are with the known provision that they have in Paradise, honored by the honor that God has honored them with.
In the gardens of bliss means: in the orchards of bliss.
On thrones facing each other means: some of them will face each other, and they will not look at each other's backs.
And His statement, A cup of flowing wine will be passed around to them, God Almighty says: Servants will pass around to them with a cup of flowing wine, visible to their eyes, not sunken in.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: A cup of flowing wine will be passed around among them. He said: A cup of running wine, and running wine is running wine.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: regarding his statement, with a cup of pure wine, he said: Every cup in the Qur’an is wine.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, who said:
m: Every cup mentioned in the Qur’an is wine.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, with a cup of pure wine, he said: Wine. And a cup among the Arabs is any vessel that contains a drink. If there is no drink in it, then it is not a cup, but it is a vessel.

x: And his saying, White, a delight to those who drink, he means by white: the cup, and because the cup is feminine, white was made feminine, and he did not say white. It was mentioned that in Abdullah's reading, it is yellow.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, white, Al-Suddi said in Abdullah’s reading: yellow.

x: And his saying there is no ghoul in it means: there is no ghoul in this wine, which means that it will not take away their minds. He says: This wine will not take away the minds of its drinkers, as the wines of the people of this world take away their minds if they drink it and drink a lot of it, as the poet said: The cup still kills us and takes the first place The Arabs say: There is no ghoul in it, “ghoul,” and ghoul have the same meaning. They raised ghoul and did not lower la because of the adjective letter that came between it and ghoul. The Arabs do the same with exoneration if they put a letter of adjectives between la and the noun, they raise the noun and do not lower it. His saying There is no ghoul in it may mean: There is nothing in it that could harm them from harm. This is because the Arabs say about a man who is afflicted with something bad, or who is afflicted with a great calamity: So-and-so has been a ghoul.
The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: It means: There is no headache in it.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Therein is no terror means: There is no headache in it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: There is no harm in it that would cause their stomachs to complain about it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: There is no ghoul in it. He said: It is wine, there is no stomach ache in it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
therein is no threat
, he said: a stomach ache.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Therein is no evil, he said: The evil is that which causes stomach pain, and the drinker of alcohol here complains of stomach pain.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: There is no ghast in it, meaning there is no stomach ache or headache in it.

x: Others said: This means that it does not affect their minds.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: There is no ghoul in it, he said: We do not assassinate their minds.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: There is no harm or discomfort in it.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Zaida, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Therein is no threat
, he said: No harm or discomfort.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Abdullah bin Buzay’ah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement,
h
therein is no threat
, he said: There is no harm or discomfort in it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: There is no sin in it. All of these sayings that we have mentioned have a basis, and that is that the ghoul in the speech of the Arabs is: that which overwhelms a person and takes him away, so everyone who is afflicted with something that he dislikes, they give him this example, and they say: Ghalat so-and-so is a ghoul. So the one who loses his mind from drinking alcohol, the one who has a stomach complaint from it, the one who has a headache from it, and the one who has suffered something unpleasant from it, all of them have been afflicted by a ghoul. If that is the case, and God Almighty has denied that the drink of Paradise contains any ghoul, then what is more appropriate to its description is to say about it as He, the Most High, said: There is no ghoul in it, thus denying all meanings of ghoul from it. More generally, it is said: There is no harm in it or any distress to its drinkers in body or mind, or anything else.

The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase nor will they be intoxicated from it. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as nor will they be intoxicated from it, with a fatha on the zay, meaning: nor will their minds be exhausted from drinking it. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as nor will they be intoxicated from it, with a kasra on the zay, meaning: nor will their drink be exhausted from drinking it. Surat al-Saffat 37:47 There is no evil therein, nor will they be intoxicated therefrom. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings and not different, so whichever one the reader recites is correct, because the drink of the people of Paradise will not run out, nor will their drinking of it intoxicate them and cause them to lose their minds.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of this.
Some of them said: It means: Their minds will not be lost.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: nor will they lose their minds. He said: Their minds will not be lost.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: nor will they be exhausted from it, he said: They will not be exhausted so that their minds will be lost.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, nor will they lose their minds he said: their minds will not be lost.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, nor will they be exhausted from it, he said: Their minds will not be exhausted.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, nor will they be drained of their blood, he said: The minds will not be drained.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Nor will they be overcome by it. He said: Their minds will not be overcome by it. This interpretation which we mentioned from those we mentioned from, whose narrators did not detail for us the reading which has this interpretation, and it may be possible that this is the interpretation of the reading of those who read it yanzifun and yanzifun both of them, and that is because the Arabs say: the man has been drained, so he is drained: if he lost his mind from drunkenness, and anzab, so he is drained, both languages are reported from them in the loss of the mind from drunkenness, and as for if the wine of the people is finished, then I have not heard of it except anzaf al-qawm with the alif. And from inzaf meaning: loss of the mind from drunkenness, the saying of al-Abird: By my life, whether you bleed or wake up, you, the family of Abjara, will be bad companions.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase nor will they be intoxicated from it.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as nor will they be intoxicated from it, with a fatha on the zay, meaning: nor will their minds be exhausted from drinking it.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as nor will they be intoxicated from it, with a kasra on the zay, meaning: nor will their drink be exhausted from drinking it.

This interpretation which we mentioned from those we mentioned from, whose narrators did not detail for us the reading which has this interpretation, and it may be possible that this is the interpretation of the reading of those who read it yanzifun and yanzifun both of them, and that is because the Arabs say: the man has been drained, so he is drained: if he lost his mind from drunkenness, and anzab, so he is drained, both languages are reported from them in the loss of the mind from drunkenness, and as for if the wine of the people is finished, then I have not heard of it except anzaf al-qawm with the alif.

x: God Almighty says: And with these sincere servants of God in Paradise are those who restrain their glances, and they are the women who restrain their glances to their husbands, and do not desire anyone other than them, and do not extend their sight to anyone other than them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And with them will be women
h
limiting their glances
to their eyes, meaning: from other than their husbands.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And with them are women
h
limiting their glances
and eyes. He said: From their husbands. Al-Harith added in his hadith: Do not seek anyone other than them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, And with them will be women restraining their glances, he said: They restrained their sight and their hearts to their husbands, and they did not desire anyone other than them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: It was also mentioned on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And with them are women
h
limiting their glances
. He said: They limit their glances to their husbands, and do not desire anyone other than them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement,
h
Limiting their glances

, he said: They do not look except at their husbands. They have limited their glances to their husbands, not as the women of this world do. His saying eye means by eye: the son of the eyes, its bones, and it is the plural of aynaa, and aynaa is the woman with wide eyes, her greatness, and she is the most beautiful of eyes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, eye, he said: The bones of the eyes.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, eye, he said: Al-Ayna’ is the large eye.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told us: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadfi al-Dimyati told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Hashim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Karima, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umm Salamah,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God, Hoor with wide, beautiful eyes (al-Waqi’ah 56:22). He said: The eye means the large eyes. The eyelashes of the houri are like the wings of an eagle.

x: And his saying,
h
As if they were hidden eggs
, the people of interpretation differed as to what they were likened to among the eggs in this statement.
Some of them said: They were likened to the inside of the egg in the whiteness, which is what is inside the shell, and that is because nothing has touched it.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement,
h
As if they were hidden eggs
, he said: As if they were the insides of eggs.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
As if they were hidden eggs
. He said: The eggs when they are peeled before being touched by hands.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
As if they were hidden eggs
, that hands had not passed over or touched, and they resembled its whiteness.

x: Others said: Rather, he likened them to the eggs that a bird incubates, which are yellow, so he likened their whiteness to that yellowness.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
As if they were hidden eggs

, he said: The eggs that are hidden by feathers, like the eggs of ostriches that have been hidden by feathers from the wind, so they are white to yellowish and as if they are flashing, so that is the hidden one.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by white in this place is pearls, and they were likened to it in their whiteness and purity.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
As if they were hidden eggs

, meaning hidden pearls. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the one who said: They are likened in their whiteness, and that no human or jinn has touched them before their husbands, to the white of the egg which is inside the shell, and that is the skin covering the yolk before it is touched by a hand or anything else, and that is undoubtedly what is hidden. As for the upper shell, the bird touches it, the hands touch it, and love encounters it. The Arabs say for everything that is protected and hidden, whether that thing is pearls, eggs, or goods, as Abu Dahbal said: She is a flower like a pearl of gold, distinguished from a hidden essence. And you say to everything that the chests conceal: I concealed it, so it is concealed. In a similar manner to what we have said, there is a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Abd al-Rahman bin Wahb told us: Muhammad bin al-Faraj al-Sadfi al-Dimyati told us, on the authority of Amr bin Hashim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Karima, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah.
m: I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about His statement,
h
As if they were hidden eggs
. He said: Their thinness is like the thinness of the skin that you saw inside the egg next to the shell, which is the gharqa’.

x: And His statement, So some of them turned to others, asking each other, God Almighty says: So some of the people of Paradise turned to others, asking each other. He says: They asked each other.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then some of them turned to others, asking each other - the people of Paradise.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then some of them will turn to others, asking questions, he said: The people of Paradise.

x: God Almighty says: A speaker from among the people of Paradise said, as some of them turned to one another, asking each other, Indeed, I had a companion.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the companion mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: That companion was a devil, and he was the one who said to him, Are you among those who believe? in the resurrection after death.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, I had a companion, he said: A devil.

x: Others said: That companion was a partner he had from among the children of Adam or a companion.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, One of them said, ‘Indeed, I had a companion * who said, ‘Are you indeed of those who believe?’ He said: It is the polytheist who has a companion in this world who is among the people of faith, so the polytheist says to him, Do you indeed believe that you will be resurrected after death? Then what if we were dust? So when they reached the Hereafter and the believer was admitted to Paradise and the polytheist was admitted to Hell, the believer looked up and saw his companion in the midst of Hell. He said, ‘By God, you were almost doomed.’

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me,
m: Atab bin Bashir said, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Furat bin Tha’laba Al-Bahrani, regarding His statement, Indeed, I had a companion, he said: Two men were partners, and eight thousand dinars came together for them. One of them had a trade and the other had no trade. The one who had a trade said to the other: You have no trade. I see myself only leaving you and dividing it between you. So he divided it between him and parted from him. Then the man bought a house for a thousand dinars that had belonged to a king who had died. He called its owner and showed it to him. He said: What do you think of this house that you bought for a thousand dinars? He said: How beautiful it is. When he left, he said: O God, my friend bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise. So he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he stayed as long as God willed him to stay. Then he married a woman for a thousand dinars, so God invited him and made him food. When he came to him, he said: I married this woman for a thousand dinars. He said: How beautiful this is. When he left, he said: O Lord, my friend married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a woman from the houris, so he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he stayed as long as God willed him to stay. Then he bought two gardens for two thousand dinars. Then he called him and showed him, and he said: I bought these two gardens. He said: How beautiful this is. When he left, he said: O Lord, my friend bought two gardens for two thousand dinars, and I ask You for two gardens from Paradise. So he gave two thousand dinars in charity. Then the Angel came to them and took them. Then he went with this charitable person and brought him into a house that pleased him. Then a woman appeared, and everything beneath her was illuminated by light. He improved it, then entered two gardens, and something about which God is All-Knowing. Then he said, How similar this is to a man who was in such-and-such a situation. He said, Then he is the one, and this house, the two gardens, and the woman are for you. He said, For I had a companion who used to say, ‘Are you indeed among those who believe?’ It was said to him, For he is in Hellfire. He said, Are you looking in? So he looked in and saw him in the midst of Hellfire. Then he said, “By God, you were almost sent back. And were it not for the grace of my Lord, you would have been among those brought forth.” . . . The verses.
b.via: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed

x: This interpretation given by Furat bin Tha'labah strengthens the reading of those who read A'innaka liman al-musaddiqin with a shaddah on the sad meaning: liman al-musaddiqin, because he is mentioning that God, the Exalted, gave him what He gave him for his charity, not for his belief. The reading of the reciters of other regions is contrary to that; rather, they read it with a light sad and a shaddah on the dal, meaning: denying his companion's belief that he will be resurrected after death, as if he said: Do you believe that you will be resurrected after your death, and that you will be rewarded for your deeds, and that you will love one another? This is indicated by God's statement:
h
When we have died and become dust and bones
, will we then indeed be recompensed? This is the correct reading according to us, and it is not permissible to go against it due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on both of them.
And the saying,
h
Are we truly to be held accountable

? means: Are we to be held accountable and rewarded after our fate has been turned into bones and our flesh into dust? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Are we truly to be recompensed? means: Are we to be rewarded for our deeds? As you judge, you will be judged.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Are we truly to be held accountable
h
Are we truly to be held accountable

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Are we truly to be held accountable

The middle of Hell

the middle of Hell
. That is, in
h
the middle of Hell

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Khalid al-Asri, he said:
m: If God had not made him know him, he would not have known him. His ink and his skin changed after him. He told us that he looked up and saw the skulls of the people, so he said: “By God, you were almost destroyed. And if it had not been for the grace of my Lord, you would have been among those brought forth.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Wazir told us: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mutraf bin Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement, Then he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire, he said: By God, if he had not recognized him, he would not have recognized him. The fire has changed his ink and his skin.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Are you seeing
? He said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it,
h
Are you seeing

me? So he looked and saw him in the middle of Hell. He said: In the middle of Hell. This reading which Al-Suddi mentioned, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to read in Mutla’un if it was preserved from him, then it is from the irregular letters, and that is because the Arabs do not affect the possessive of nouns if they are connected to an agent in the plural or singular. They hardly say you are speaking to me nor you two are speaking to me nor you all are speaking to me nor you all are speaking to me nor you all are speaking to me but rather they say you are speaking to me and you two are speaking to me and you all are speaking to me. And if one of them said that, he said it by mistake, imagining it: you speak to me and you two are speaking to me and you all are speaking to me, as the poet said: I do not know, and my suspicion is that they handed me over to my people. He said: Muslim me. This is not the proper way of speaking, rather the proper way of speaking is Muslim me. But if the speech is apparent and not connected to the subject, then they may add, and they may not, so it is said: This one is speaking to your brother, and the one speaking to your brother, and these two are speaking to your brother, and the two speaking to your brother, and these are speaking to your brother, and the ones speaking to your brother? And the addition is chosen in the implied word connected to the subject because the two letters become connected to one another, like a single letter. And his saying, By God,
h
you almost destroyed me
, means: When he saw his companion in the fire, he said, By God,
h
you almost destroyed me
in this world by turning me away from belief in resurrection, reward, and punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
You almost destroyed me

. He said: To destroy me. It is said from this: So-and-so destroyed so-and-so: if he destroyed him, and so-and-so was destroyed: if he perished, as Al-A’sha said. In the flood, I feared death, while many have been returned to their families without being thrown He means by his saying: How many were returned: How many were lost.

evidence.text: He said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it, Are you seeing me?

This reading which Al-Suddi mentioned, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to read in Mutla’un if it was preserved from him, then it is from the irregular letters, and that is because the Arabs do not affect the possessive of nouns if they are connected to an agent in the plural or singular.

x: And his saying: And had it not been for the grace of my Lord,
h
I would have been among those brought forth
. He says: And had it not been for God’s blessing upon me with His guidance and the success in believing in the resurrection after death,
h
I would have been among those brought forth
with you in God’s punishment.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h

: meaning in the punishment of God.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
I would have been among those brought forth
, he said: Among those being punished.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what this believer said to whom God gave him what He gave him of His honor in His Paradise, out of His pleasure with what He gave him in it: Are we not to die?
Except our first death He says: Are we not going to die except for our first death in this world, and we are not going to be punished He says: We are not going to be punished after we enter Paradise.

Indeed, this is the great attainment. He says: This honor that God has given us in Paradise, that we will not be tormented or die, is the great salvation from what we were fearing God's punishment in this world, and the attainment of what we were hoping for in it through our faith and obedience to our Lord.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Are we not to die?...to his statement, the great success. He said: This is the statement of the people of Paradise. And His statement,
h
For the like of this let the workers work

, God Almighty says: For the like of this which these believers have been given of honor in the Hereafter, let the workers work for themselves in this world, so that they may attain what these people have attained through obedience to their Lord.

x: God the Almighty says: Is this what I have given to these believers, whose characteristics I have described, of My honor in Paradise, and the bliss I have provided for them therein better, or what I have prepared for the people of Hell of Zaqqum? By nuzul means bounty, and there are two expressions for it: nazul and nazul. It is said about food that has a profit: it is food that has nazul and nazul. And His statement,
h
Or the tree of Zaqqum indicates that when God the Almighty revealed this verse
, the polytheists said: How can trees grow in fire, while fire burns trees?
So God said: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers, meaning for those polytheists who said what they said about it.

c: Then He informed them
m: of the description of this tree, saying: It is a tree that springs forth from the bottom of Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Is that a better lodging or the tree of Zaqqum? until he reached at the bottom of Hellfire. He said: When he mentioned the tree of Zaqqum, the oppressors were tempted and said: Your companion has informed you that there is a tree in Hellfire, and fire eats trees. So God revealed what you hear: It is a tree that grows at the bottom of Hellfire, nourished by fire and from it it was created.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Abu Jahl said:
m: When the verse, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum was revealed, he said: You know it in the speech of the Arabs: I will bring it to you. So he called a slave girl and said: Bring me dates and butter. He said: Here, swallow yourselves, for this is the Zaqqum that Muhammad is frightening you with. So God revealed its interpretation: Is that better as a lodging or the tree of Zaqqum? Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. He said: For Abu Jahl and his companions.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers, he said: Abu Jahl’s statement: The zaqqum is only dates and butter, I swallow it.

x: And His statement,
h
Its fruit is like the heads of devils

, God Almighty says: It is as if the fruit of this tree, meaning the tree of Zaqqum in its ugliness and hideousness, is like the heads of devils in its ugliness. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading, it is a tree growing at the bottom of Hell.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Its emergence was like the heads of devils
, he said: He likened it to that.

x: What is the point of likening the growth of this tree to the heads of devils in ugliness? We do not know the extent of the ugliness of the heads of devils. Rather, the thing is represented by the thing as a definition from the represented to the represented, the close similarity of the represented one to the other, while the represented one knows both things, or one of them. It is known that those who were addressed by this verse from the polytheists did not know the tree of Zaqqum, nor the heads of devils, nor did they see them, nor either of them.

As for the tree of Zaqqum, God Almighty described it to them and made it clear so that they knew what it is and what its description is. He said to them, A tree that springs forth from the bottom of Hellfire, its fruit as if it were the heads of devils. So He did not leave them in the dark about it. As for his comparison of its fruit as the heads of devils, I say that each of them has an understandable aspect: One of them is that it is likened to the heads of devils in the manner that the addressees of the verse have been using among themselves. This is because people have been using it in their exaggeration when one of them wants to exaggerate in making something ugly, he says: As if it were a devil.

This is one of the sayings. The second is that it is likened to the head of a snake known among the Arabs and called a devil, and it is a snake that has a crest, as mentioned, and its face is ugly to look at. This is what the rajaz poet meant when he said: Anjar swears when I swear like the devil of Hamaat I know

And Ajeez narrates. The third: That it is like a plant known as the heads of devils, and it was mentioned that it has an ugly head. Then they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it. God Almighty says: These polytheists, for whom God made this tree a trial, will eat from this tree, which is the tree of Zaqqum, and fill their bellies with its Zaqqum.

God Almighty says: Then for them is a mixture of scalding water. Then for these polytheists, what they eat from this tree, the tree of Zaqqum, is a mixture, from the Arabs’ saying: So-and-so mixed his food with scalding water, so he mixes it with scalding water. The scalding water is hot water, which is heated until its heat is extreme, and its root is maf’ul, which is converted to fa’il. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then they will have a mixture of scalding water
, meaning: a mixture.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then they will have a mixture of scalding water
means: drinking scalding water on the Zaqqum.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then they will have a mixture of scalding water
. He said: A mixture of scalding water.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Then they will have a mixture of scalding water
over it. He said: Mixture means mingling, which is blending.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Then they will have a mixture of scalding water
, he said: Scalding water will be mixed for them with pus from what makes their eyes pus, and pus from their oozing blood from what comes out of their bodies.

x: And His statement,
h
Then their return will be to Hellfire
, God Almighty says: Then their return and destiny will be to Hellfire.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:

, and he recited this verse: They will circulate between it and scalding water (al-Rahman 55:44).

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Then their return will surely be to Hellfire
, he said in Abdullah’s reading,
h
Then their return will surely be to Hellfire

(al-Furqan 25:24) Yunus told me, he said:

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,

And We had certainly sent among them warners. Then see how was the end of those who were warned. He says: So reflect and understand what was the end of those whom Our prophets warned, and what their situation became, and what followed their disbelief in God. Did We not destroy them and make them an example for the servants and a lesson for those after them?
And His statement,
h
Except the chosen servants of God

, the Almighty says: So see how was the end of those who were warned, except for the servants of God whom We made sincere in belief in God and His messengers. He excluded the servants of God from those who were warned, because the meaning of the statement is: So see how We destroyed those who were warned, except for the believing servants of God. Therefore, it was appropriate to exclude them from them. And similar to what we said about His statement,
h
Except the sincere servants of God
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement,
h
Except the sincere servants of God
, he said: Those whom God has chosen.

x: God the Almighty says: Noah called upon Us, asking Us to destroy his people, saying: My Lord, I have called upon my people night and day, * But my call has only increased them in flight
r
. . until His saying: My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller
r
. And His statement:
h
The best of responders
means:
h
The best of responders

we were to him when he called upon Us, so We answered his call, and destroyed his people. And We saved him and his family meaning: the people of Noah who boarded the ship with him. We have mentioned them previously, and explained the scholars’ disagreement over their number. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And Noah called upon Us, and excellent is the respondent. He said: God answered him.

x: And his saying, from the great distress, means: from the harm and distress that he experienced from the disbelievers, and from the distress of the flood and drowning by which the people of Noah perished.

c: As Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And We saved him and his family from the great distress, he said: from drowning.

x: And His statement,
h
And We made his descendants the survivors

, means: And We made the descendants of Noah the ones who remained on the earth after the destruction of Lot, and that is because all people from the destruction of Noah until today are the descendants of Noah, so the Persians and the Arabs are the descendants of Sam, son of Noah, and the Turks, Slavs, and Khazars are the descendants of Japheth, son of Noah, and the Sudanese are the descendants of Ham, son of Noah, and this is what the traces came with, and the scholars said.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Ibn Uthma told us, he said: Saeed ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement,
h
And We made his descendants the survivors
, he said: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We made his descendants the survivors
, he said: So all people are from the descendants of Noah.

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We made his descendants the survivors
, he said: Only the descendants of Noah remained.

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
And We left for him among later generations

, and We kept for him, meaning for Noah, a beautiful memory and good praise among later generations, meaning: among those who came after him from among the people who remember him by it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement,
h
And We left for him among later generations
, meaning: he will be remembered with goodness.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And We left for him among later generations
, he said: We made a tongue of truth for all the prophets.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And We left for him among later generations
, he said: God left for him good praise among later generations.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We left for him among later generations
, he said: Good praise.

x: And his saying "
h
Peace be upon Noah among the worlds
" means: a security from God to Noah among the worlds that no one would speak ill of him, and peace is raised with the preposition 'ala.

Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa used to say: its meaning is: and we left for him among the others, "Peace be upon Noah" meaning we left this word for him, just as you say you read from the Qur'an, Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, so the sentence is in the accusative case, and you raise it with the preposition lam. Likewise, peace be upon Noah, you raise it with the preposition 'ala, and it is in the interpretation of the accusative case. He said: If it had been: we left for him peace, it would have been correct.
And His statement,
h
Thus do We reward the doers of good

, the Almighty says: Indeed, as We did with Noah as a reward for his obedience to Us and his patience in the face of the harm caused to his people in Our pleasure, And We saved him and his family from the great distress, and made his descendants the survivors, and We kept him, as praise for others, Thus do We reward those who do good, obey Us, comply with Our command, and are patient in the face of the harm caused to them by Us.
And His saying,
h
He was one of Our believing servants
, means: Noah was one of Our servants who believed in Us, so he made Us one, devoted worship to Us, and singled Us out as divinity.
And His statement,
h
Then We drowned the others

, God Almighty says: Then, when We saved Noah and his family from the great distress, We drowned those who remained of his people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
Then We drowned the others
. He said: God saved him and those with him in the ship, and drowned the rest of his people.

x: God Almighty says: And indeed, among the followers of Noah were those who followed his way and his religion. And God was with Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what I said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And among his followers is Abraham
, meaning: among the people of his religion.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And among his followers is Abraham
, he said: On the path and Sunnah of Noah.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And among his followers is Abraham
, he said: On his path and his Sunnah.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And among his followers is Abraham
. He said: Of his religion and his faith.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And among his followers is Abraham

, he said: Among the people of his religion. Some Arabists have claimed that the meaning of this is: And among the followers of Muhammad are Abraham. He said that this contradicts his statement, And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring
r
meaning: We carried the offspring of those who are from him, so He made them their offspring, and they preceded them.

x: And his saying,
h
When he came to his Lord with a sound heart
, God Almighty says: When Abraham came to his Lord with a heart free from polytheism, devoted to monotheism.

m: h
When he came to his Lord with a sound heart
and God from polytheism.

m: regarding His statement,
h
When he came to his Lord with a sound heart
, he said: Sound from polytheism.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With a sound heart. He said: There is no doubt.

x: Others said about that as follows:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Uthman bin Ali told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: O my sons, do not curse. Have you not seen that Abraham never cursed anything? Then God said,
h
When he came to his Lord with a sound heart

x: And his saying,
h
When he said to his father and his people
, ‘What do you worship?’ He says: When he said, meaning Abraham, to his father and his al-Nas 114:What do you worship?
And his saying,
h
Do you desire gods other than God
? He says, Do you desire a false god other than God?

God Almighty says, informing us of what Abraham said to his father and his al-Nas 114:Then what do you think of the Lord of the worlds? He says: What do you think, O people, that He will do to you if you meet Him and you have worshipped other than Him?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: What then do you think of the Lord of the worlds? He said: If you meet Him and you have worshipped other than Him.

x: And his saying,
h
So he looked at the stars and said

, 'Indeed, I am sick.' He mentioned that his people were people of astrology, so he saw a star rise, so he bandaged his head and said, I am afflicted. His people were fleeing from the plague, so he wanted them to leave him in the house of their gods and leave it, so that he would oppose them to it and break it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then he looked at the stars and said
, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’ He said: They said to him while he was in the house of their gods: Go out, and he said: I am plagued. So they left him for fear of the plague.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab,
m: h
Then he looked at the stars and said
, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’ He saw a star rise.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: that he saw a star rise and said,
h
I am sick
. He said: He plotted against the Prophet of God about his religion, and he said,
h
I am sick

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Then he looked at the stars and said
, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’ They said to Abraham while he was in the house of their gods: Come out with us. He said to them: I am stricken with disease. So they left him for fear that he would infect them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on the authority of his father, regarding the statement of God,
h
Then he looked at the stars and said

, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’ He said: Their king sent to him and said, Tomorrow is our festival, so come with us. He said: So he looked at a star and said, That star has never risen except that it has risen with an illness for me. So he said, Indeed, I am ill.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
Then he looked at the stars and said

, ‘Indeed, I am ill,’ meaning God’s words, So they turned away from him, fleeing. His statement, Indeed, I am ill, means stabbed, or because of an illness from which they would flee when they heard about it. Abraham only wanted them to leave him so that he could achieve what he wanted from their idols. There is a difference of opinion about the reason why Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:
h
I am sick
, while it is true.
“It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Abraham only told three lies.”

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Usamah told us, he said: Hisham told me, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abraham did not lie except three times, two for the sake of God: his saying: ‘
h
I am sick
,’ and his saying: ‘Rather, their chief did it,’ and my saying about Sarah: ‘She is my sister.’”

c: Saeed bin Yahya told us: My father told us: Muhammad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Ibrahim never lied about anything except three things.’ Then he mentioned something similar.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: Abraham did not lie except three times: his saying,
h
I am sick
, and his saying, Rather, this chief of them did it
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 63)
, and he only said it as a sermon, and his saying when the king asked him, and he said, My sister to Sarah, and she was his wife.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, who said:
m: Abraham only told three lies: two about God and one about himself. As for the two, they were his saying,
h
I am sick
, and his saying, Rather, this chief of them did it
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 63)
, and his story about Sarah, and he mentioned her story and the story of the king.

x: Others said: His saying,
h
I am sick

, is an ambiguous statement, meaning that everyone who is on the verge of death is sick, even if he was not obviously sick when he said it. The report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, contradicts this statement, and the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the truth and no other.
His statement,
h
So they turned away from him

, retreating. He says: So they turned away from Abraham, fearing that the disease that he was mentioned to have would infect them. It was also narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Zakariya, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, I am sick, meaning I am plagued, so turn away from it and flee. Saeed said: Fleeing from the plague is ancient.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: So they turned away they retreated from him running back they set out.

x: And His statement,
h
He turned to their gods
, God Almighty says: So
h
he turned to their gods

after they had left him and turned away. I think that the origin of that is from their saying: So-and-so turned away from so-and-so: if he deviated from him, so its meaning, if that is the case, is that he turned away from his people and went out with them to their gods, as Adi bin Zaid said: When evasion is of no use and only honesty and sincerity are of use What he means by his saying: Evasion is of no use is neutrality. As for the people of interpretation, they interpreted it to mean so he turned away.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
He turned to their gods
: meaning,
h
he turned to their gods
. He said: He went.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He turned to their gods
, he said: He went.

x: And His saying, And he said, 'Why do you not eat? What is the matter with you that you do not speak?' This is report from God about what Abraham said to the gods. There is something omitted in the speech that the speech indicated without mentioning it, which is that he brought the food to her but did not see her eating, so he said to her, Why do you not eat? When he did not see her eating, he said to her, Why do you not speak? mocking her. And he mentioned that he did the same to her, and we mentioned the report of that before.
Qatada said about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then he said, ‘Why do you not eat?’ He asked them to speak, Why do you not speak?

x: God Almighty says: So he attacked the gods of his people, striking them with his right hand and breaking them with an axe in his hand.
